disposition: Suitable for a bounded isolated schematic study only.

timing.conditions: 3.3 V column; -40..125 C; use Section 7's specified 3.3 +/-0.3 V measurement conditions, including 50 pF.

flip_flop.reset: PRE_N high permits CLR_N low to force Q low regardless of CLK/D. Both asynchronous controls low is nonstable. No separate removal-time guarantee is inferred.

facts.propagation_conditions: VCC 3.3 +/-0.3 V; -40..125 C; CL 50 pF and specified test load.
VCC 3.3 +/-0.3 V; -40..125 C; CL 50 pF and specified test load.

topology_inference.READY: At a valid ACK rising edge, capture NOT ARM. QUAL_OK low asynchronously clears READY.
topology_inference.defaults: ARM, QUAL_OK and ACK each have a 10k pulldown. Retain R40 directly at translator OE.
topology_inference.power: All three logic devices use +3V3 with separate local bypass. PRE_N connects directly to +3V3; Q_N and inverter NC remain no-connect.
topology_inference.act03_difference: ACK while ARM high clears READY and disables. ACT-03 ignores acknowledgement while armed.
topology_inference.startup: The eventual qualification circuit must hold QUAL_OK low through supply startup and until reset/edge constraints are satisfied. The pulldown alone is not a characterized power-on reset.
topology_inference.held_levels: After a valid clear, held ACK or ARM cannot set READY; recovery alone cannot do so. This statement assumes valid rails, adequate fault duration and valid transitions.
topology_inference.missing_inputs: QUAL_OK and ACK are unimplemented, default-low functional ports, with no chosen harness or MCU source.

acceptance_holds: QUAL_OK must encode independently reviewed rails, receiver readiness, stop and fresh-command watchdog qualification; none is implemented here.
A too-short QUAL_OK-low pulse can leave READY set and allow output to return after the pulse.
ACK/ARM near each other, reset release near ACK, contact bounce, slow edges, analog brownout and propagation races are excluded from functional proof.
Do not assume an initial latch state or guaranteed behavior between zero supply and the valid operating range.
Ioff conditions at zero supply do not establish arbitrary supply-ramp isolation or protect an unpowered remote actuator.
No end-to-end stopping time, glitch suppression, single-fault tolerance or production acceptance is established.
native_validation: Separate root-owned native delta verification; this source review does not assert its result.
